lf-dial.description: A control that sets how much of the page shows: Skim shows the lede, the gists and the headings above them, Read the page as written, and Everything also opens every closed detail.
lf-dial.x-instructions: Write it empty with a stable id, after the page's title and lede, on a page long enough that a reader might want only its conclusions. It governs the nearest tab or part containing it, or the whole main. Skim is only as good as the gists: mark `.gist` the passages that give a reader on a quick pass the page's argument and anything they must act on, reading coherently in order; a section with nothing for that reader takes no gist and folds whole (the detail package's author instructions).
lf-dial.x-example:
Why checkout latency doubled

A cache key change on Tuesday sent every checkout to the database.

Cause

The 4.2 release added the currency to the cart cache key, so no cached cart matched.

Hit rate fell from 94% to 3% within a minute of the deploy, and p99 rose from 180 ms to 410 ms.

The key, before and after 
cart:{user}  →  cart:{user}:{currency}

.gist.description: A block that says what a passage concludes, readable without the text around it; with `lf-dial` at Skim, the lede, the gists and the headings above them are all that shows.
.gist.x-example:
Cause

The cache key changed, so no cached cart matched.

Hit rate fell from 94% to 3% within a minute of the deploy.
